test_title: PYST 70: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

The philosopher remarked that, had the syllogism been valid, the paradox would not have arisen".

options.text: The philosopher said, "If the syllogism is valid, the paradox does not arise."
The philosopher said, "Had the syllogism been valid, the paradox would not arise."
The philosopher said, "Had the syllogism been valid, the paradox would not have arisen."
The philosopher said, "If syllogism is valid, paradox should not arise."

solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Had the syllogism been valid, the paradox would not have arisen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **third conditional**, which is used to talk about hypothetical or unreal situations in the past.
 
• In the third conditional, the structure is **"If + past perfect, would have + past participle."**
 
• The phrase "Had the syllogism been valid" is a conditional clause that uses an inverted structure, omitting "if."
 
• The phrase "the paradox would not have arisen" is the result clause, which follows the correct third conditional format.

Correct sentence: *The philosopher said, **"Had the syllogism been valid, the paradox would not have arisen."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1st Conditional Sentence:**

 
 
• **Structure:** If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.
 
• **Usage:** Describes real or possible situations in the future with likely outcomes.
 
 
 
• **2nd Conditional Sentence:**

 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Simple, would + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If I were rich, I would travel the world.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to unreal or hypothetical situations in the present or future.
 
 
 
• **3rd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
 
• **Example:** If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to unreal past situations and their imagined outcomes.
